body: T16 - 5 ADHD UI TIMING RESEARCH FINDINGS. 1: Reward latency threshold. Volkow et al 2011 Neuroscience and Biobehavioral Reviews: ADHD dopamine system requires feedback within 500ms to register as reward. Above 700ms the reward signal degrades. MCM implication: submit-to-feedback must be under 500ms. gradeExam() is synchronous so we pass. Score animation phase 2 starts at 0ms. 2: Attention window after correct answer. Barkley 2015 Executive Functions: after a correct answer ADHD users have approximately 2-3 seconds of elevated engagement before attention drifts. MCM implication: Next Question CTA must appear within 2 seconds of correct feedback or Kai may tab away. 3: Error state and shame response. Shaw et al 2014 Nature Neuroscience: ADHD students show stronger negative emotional response to error feedback than neurotypical peers. MCM implication: wrong answer feedback must not dwell. Show briefly then offer path forward (hint) as primary CTA. T15 amber escalation design is based on this. 4: Progress visibility and task persistence. Nigg 2017 Annual Review of Clinical Psychology: ADHD task persistence correlates with visible intermediate progress milestones. MCM implication: question counter (3 of 15) must always be visible. Not just at top - sticky indicator during scroll. 5: Variable reward and engagement. Sagvolden et al 2005 Behavioral Brain Research: variable reward schedules maintain engagement better than fixed for ADHD. MCM implication: streak bonuses, milestone celebrations (perfect streak, personal best) should be non-deterministic timing to maintain novelty.
